Thanks for pasting the spreadsheet. Before anything else, one detail stood out: about a third of the rows have no "Date back." That could mean a few different problems, and each would lead to building something different. So I'd like to understand what "coming back" means in your seed library.

With tools or books, the same item goes out and the same item returns. Seed libraries often work differently. Someone borrows a packet of tomato seeds, grows them, and months later brings back seeds they saved from their own plants. Sometimes that's more than they took, sometimes none at all if the crop failed. If yours works like that, the right tool looks less like a checkout list and more like a record of who's growing what and what you can expect back at harvest. If people really do return the same unused packets, a much simpler sign-out sheet might be all you need.

When someone borrows seeds from your library, what do you hope comes back, and roughly when?
